entities.summary: Karl von Miltitz, a papal nuncio, played a pivotal role in European politics during the 16th century. Born into a noble family in what is now Germany, Miltitz's rise to prominence was influenced by his appointment as a Mainz Cathedral canon. As a trusted advisor to the Holy Roman Emperor, Charles V, Miltitz facilitated the emperor's efforts to consolidate power in Europe. His diplomatic efforts also contributed to the Protestant Reformation, as he supported Martin Luther's theological ideas. In 1529, Miltitz died, leaving behind a legacy as a key figure in the tumultuous politics of the Holy Roman Empire. His commitment to the Catholic Church and the emperor's authority helped shape the course of European history, leaving an indelible mark on the continent's religious and political landscape. The Protestant Reformation, which Miltitz supported, transformed the religious and cultural landscape of Europe, leaving a lasting impact on art, literature, and society.
